tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H4): Token-stationary one-launch FP16x3 tcgen05 kernel, fp32 h in TMEM, per-batch counters, for N <= 18944 (S+M rows). 1) Start from the #129 lineage-M engine (read_example solx_129_token_stationary_tcgen05.cu): SW128 descriptors, kind::f16 idesc, elect.sync issue, release/acquire counters with departure reset, gelu2, cooperative launch at 1 CTA/SM, 512 threads. 2) Tokens per CTA t = ceil16(N/148) capped at 96 (12544 tokens -> 96 x 131 CTAs; 6272 -> 48; 3136 -> 32; 784/1568 -> 16). A CTA's tokens may straddle 2 batches (HW=196): keep two batch slots as in #129. 3) Phase 0: every CTA converts 1/G of W1 and W2 into exact fp16 hi/lo SW128 images in a torch.empty workspace, computes part of b2' = b2 + W2.gb, then bumps one counter. The x tile lands by bulk copy and is split hi/lo in registers into the B tile. 4) GEMM1 swap-AB D1[hidden 128-block][t]: 4 blocks, with the 3 products as K-concatenated passes; W1 hi/lo streamed in 64 KB blocks through a 2-stage ring. Epilogue: + b1, gelu2, per-channel sumsq, fp32 h back into TMEM with tcgen05.st, red.add into gsum[b][512], per-batch counter. 5) After the batch wait: s_b = 1 + gw*G/(mean G + eps) with exact sqrt and div; h' = h*s_b split hi/lo into smem per 128-k chunk; GEMM2 D2[out 128][t] with hi*hi in one accumulator and the cross terms in a second one placed in freed h columns (TMEM <= 512); W2 hi/lo streamed per 64 KB k-chunk. out = A + B + b2', stored coalesced [token][128] with evict_last. 6) Rows with N > 18944 route to the r0-simt-3k path unchanged. One launch per call; torch.empty is the only torch call in run(). 7) Add %globaltimer phase stamps (weights ready, x landed, GEMM1, epilogue, batch wait, GEMM2, store) at 1,28,28, 4,28,28, 2,56,56, 4,56,56 and 16,28,28, and a SASS count of epilogue instructions per element. 8) run_tests all 14 rows; log err/tol per row over 10 rounds. If the 12544-token rows miss the gate, measure the fallback configuration t = 64 with more CTAs (2 rounds) and ship the better one. Success: All 9 rows with N <= 18944 pass with err/tol <= 0.8; 12544-token rows <= 21 us rented, 6272 <= 15 us, 784 <= 13 us. Refuted if: After the fallback configuration the 12544-token rows exceed 30 us rented, and the stamps show weight landing plus batch wait above 50% of the kernel time (a structural cost, not a bug). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). A missed gate or success line is not a reason to stop: switch to the best configuration your own probes found (or the experiment's next variant), build it into a full kernel and measure it with run_tests, and use the rest of the budget on it. Hand in a measured kernel that implements this experiment's design on at least one workload (others may fall back); the r0 baseline or the unchanged parent is not a valid candidate unless a measured hardware fact rules the design out (name it, with the probe's number). Record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Keep the kernel copy-like (memory-bound): the portal locks the SM clock lower than the test bench and penalises extra SM work per byte (the problem card). Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic / bulk-reduce target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); any h ring or scratch is reused only within one call, never across calls; grid, cluster or per-batch counters live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only (tcgen05 does not build for LOCAL); TMA descriptors encoded every call; no state kept between calls (no converted or split weights, no cached outputs) except shape-keyed attributes set to one maximal value; cache hints only on our own workspace buffers, never on hidden_states, the weights or the output; cuobjdump -res-usage STACK 0 on the shipped build; 10-round fp64 precision log on every shipped row (err/tol).

Experiment E2 (tests H11): S-row hidden-slice fan-out: token tiles x hidden slices, one grid barrier, red.add split-K GEMM2, for N <= 6272. 1) Grid = token tiles x hidden slices, about 112-148 CTAs, one wave. Start from 784 = 7 tiles of 112 x 16 slices of 32; 1568 = 14 x 8 of 64 (or 16 x 8 at 98); 3136 = 28 x 4 of 128; 6272 = 56 x 2 of 256. Tune the slice count per shape (dispatch on shape only). 2) Each CTA bulk-loads its own fp32 slices W1[slice,:] and W2[:,slice] plus x, b1, gw, gb at entry and converts them to fp16 hi/lo SW128 smem images itself: no workspace and no weight counter. 3) GEMM1 FP16x3 (non-swapped M = 128 tokens with masked rows, N = slice, K = 128 as 3 K-concatenated products, or swap-AB if the slice is 128), + b1, gelu2 from #129, sumsq red.add into gsum[b][512]. Before the barrier, the slice-0 CTA of each tile stores b2' = b2 + W2.gb into its out rows: do not rely on the harness zero-fill. 4) One monotonic grid counter (the #129 form; departure reset). 5) Then s_b for its slice, x2' = h*s_b split hi/lo, GEMM2 partial D2[tokens][128 out] with K = slice (separate cross-term accumulator), red.global.add.v4.f32 into out. If the red.add tail exceeds 1.5 us at 16 slices, try 8 slices or a cluster DSMEM reduction (allowed: small one-wave grid). 6) Other rows route to r0-simt-3k. 7) Phase stamps at 1,28,28, 8,14,14, 4,28,28, 16,14,14, 2,56,56 and 32,14,14; err/tol log per row over 10 rounds; run_tests all 14. Success: The 6 rows with N <= 6272 pass with err/tol <= 0.8; 1,28,28 <= 9 us rented, 3136-token rows <= 11 us, 6272-token rows <= 14 us. Refuted if: 1,28,28 exceeds 12 us rented (1.5x the 8 us projection) after tuning the slice count, and the stamps attribute the excess to the chain (ingest, barrier, red.add), not to a bug. Experiment E3 (tests H10): L: persistent single launch, h stored to a per-CTA L2 workspace ring with evict_last, re-read one round later; correct for all 14 rows. 0) Probe first, <= 3 minutes: after a harness-style 2xL2 zero-fill, 148 CTAs write 38 and then 76 MB with st.global.L2::cache_hint evict_last, cross a grid counter, then each CTA re-reads its own bytes (cp.async.bulk). Report read-back TB/s and total time against a DRAM-only control. 1) Kernel: 148 CTAs at 1 CTA/SM, cooperative launch, static batch-major schedule of 128-token tiles. Round r: GEMM1 FP16x3 of this CTA's tile (x by bulk copy and register split; W1 hi/lo images from a phase-0 conversion, as in #129) -> + b1, gelu2, sumsq red.add per batch, per-batch counter -> store h (fp32, or fp16 hi/lo, your choice; 2 KB/token) into this CTA's workspace slot (r mod 2) with evict_last. Then GEMM2 of the tile from round r-1: wait for its batches' counters (they should already be complete), re-land the CTA's own h tile from L2, h' = h*s_b split hi/lo into smem (or fold s_b into a per-batch W2'_b if you store hi/lo), GEMM2 with a separate cross-term accumulator, out + b2' stored with evict_last. Prefetch the next x tile behind GEMM2. Workspace from torch.empty; counters self-reset. 2) The same kernel must be correct for all 14 rows (S/M = one round plus a drain). 3) Stamps per round at 32,28,28, 16,56,56 and 64,56,56: GEMM1, epilogue, h store, wait, h re-land, GEMM2. SASS count per epilogue element. 4) run_tests all 14; err/tol per row over 10 rounds. If the probe refutes L2 residency, still ship the same structure (DRAM fallback, about 5 KB/token) and report its time. Success: All 14 rows pass with err/tol <= 0.8; 64,56,56 <= 165 us rented, 16,56,56 <= 45 us, 32,28,28 <= 30 us. Refuted if: The probe's read-back runs under 10 TB/s aggregate (H10 refuted) and the kernel exceeds 200 us at 64,56,56 (1.5x its ~130 us projection). Experiment E4 (tests H13): L: persistent batch-aligned rounds with fp32 h in TMEM and per-batch counters (on-chip h, no h in memory). 1) Same engine family as E1 (#129 lineage-M template), but persistent: 148 CTAs at 1 CTA/SM, cooperative launch. A round holds whole batches only: HW=3136 -> 6 batches (18816 tokens, 128-token tiles with masking, ~147 CTAs busy); HW=784 -> 24 batches. Tiles that straddle batches keep two batch slots. Choose tile 128 (512 TMEM columns of h, GEMM2 accumulators in columns freed by converting h blocks to smem) or tile 96 (128 columns free); measure both if time allows. 2) Per round: GEMM1 FP16x3 (W1 hi/lo images from a phase-0 conversion and counter; 64 KB ring) -> + b1, gelu2, sumsq red.add into gsum[b][512] (each batch's slot zeroed before its round by a designated CTA, with ordering argued) -> per-batch counter -> s_b -> h' chunks split hi/lo into smem -> GEMM2 with a separate cross-term accumulator -> out + b2' stored with evict_last. Prefetch the next round's x tile during the wait and GEMM2. Counters monotonic per call with departure reset. 3) Rows with N <= 18944 may run as one round (a competitor to E1); all 14 rows must be correct. 4) Stamps per round at 32,28,28, 16,56,56 and 64,56,56 (GEMM1, epilogue, wait, GEMM2, store) and the MMA-warp idle fraction. 5) run_tests all 14; err/tol per row over 10 rounds. Success: All 14 rows pass with err/tol <= 0.8; <= 15 us per 128-token round, i.e. 64,56,56 <= 170 us rented and 32,28,28 <= 30 us. Refuted if: After the fallback tile choice a round takes more than 22 us at 128 tokens (64,56,56 > 240 us rented), with the stamps showing serial epilogue plus wait as the cause.
